title: Stale jit binary misreads newer repo data instead of failing fast on format mismatch
description:
Friction observed while lead-driving epic 2821e177 (2026-07-03, session 2).

An installed `jit` binary older than the repository's data produces opaque, misleading failures instead of a version-mismatch diagnosis. Two incidents in one session while dogfooding storage/validation changes:

1. After the live repo migrated `gates.json` -> `gates.toml`, the stale PATH binary failed every command touching the registry with "Failed to read file: .jit/gates.json" (exit 4) — nothing hinted that the DATA had moved on and the BINARY was behind.
2. After `invariants.toml` bindings moved to `@/rule/...`/`@/gate/...` addresses, the stale binary's string-matching drift check reported 4 phantom enforcement-drift findings on a perfectly green repo.

Both read as repo corruption or regressions; the fix each time was `cargo install --path crates/jit`. `index.json` already carries `schema_version`, but the gates-file relocation and the binding-format change did not bump anything a binary checks.

Proposal: a repo-format capability marker the binary verifies on startup — e.g. a `format` (or per-store schema) version in `index.json` or `config.toml` that is bumped whenever an on-disk layout or interpretation changes, with old binaries failing fast: "this repository's data format (N) is newer than this jit binary supports (M); rebuild/upgrade jit". Writing with a NEWER binary into an older-format repo may migrate or bump as today.

Acceptance: running a deliberately outdated binary against a newer-format repo yields the explicit mismatch error (non-zero, single line, names both versions) instead of a file-read error or wrong validation verdicts.
